papers.title: Thermostable Carbohydrate-Active Enzymes for High-Temperature Biomass Conversion: From Molecular Design to Process Integration.
papers.abstract: High-temperature processing of carbohydrate-rich biomass, including starch liquefaction and lignocellulose saccharification, can improve sugar yields, reduce contamination risks, and facilitate integration with thermochemical pretreatments. However, the operational stability of native carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) at 60-90 °C remains a major bottleneck for efficient and economically viable biorefineries, and existing reviews rarely integrate multiscale molecular mechanisms with process-relevant engineering strategies. This review systematically examines the multiscale basis of thermost
papers.summary: This review examines the molecular and structural basis of thermostability in carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) and how these properties can be engineered for high-temperature biomass conversion processes such as starch liquefaction and lignocellulose saccharification. It integrates multiscale mechanistic insights—from protein structure and dynamics to process-level engineering—to address the stability bottleneck at 60–90 °C in biorefineries. The work aims to connect molecular design strategies with practical process integration for more efficient and economical biomass conversion.

papers.title: Design and Evolution of an Orthogonal HaloTag for Multiplexed Labeling in Cells.
papers.abstract: The self-labeling protein HaloTag is used to install a wide variety of functional small molecules in cells and living organisms with exquisite specificity with respect to cell type and subcellular localization. HaloTag is a core part of many biotechnology-based tools for sensing, tracking, and manipulating biological systems with a high degree of spatial and temporal control. Due to the limitations of fluorescent proteins and other self-labeling proteins, most of these tools have historically been restricted to a single channel. In this work, we used structure-guided rational design and direct
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors used structure-guided rational design to engineer an orthogonal HaloTag variant that can be labeled independently of the original HaloTag, enabling multiplexed small-molecule labeling in cells. This expands the toolkit for simultaneously tracking or manipulating multiple proteins with high spatial and temporal control.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Potential of the Edible Seaweed Pterocladiella capillacea: Bioactivity Coupled LC-MS/MS, Metabolomics Annotation, Validation, and Network Pharmacology.
papers.abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder with a global impact, highlighting an urgent need for effective dietary therapeutic agents for the development of brain-healthy functional foods and medicines. This study focuses on the edible red alga Pterocladiella capillacea from Zhanjiang, China, investigating its anti-neuronal injury activity, active principles, and underlying mechanisms. Methods: Based on antioxidant and neuroprotection evaluations and column fractioning, bioactivity-coupled liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (Bio-LC-MS/MS) was emplo
papers.summary: This study investigates the edible red seaweed Pterocladiella capillacea for neuroprotective compounds relevant to Alzheimer's disease. Using bioactivity-guided fractionation coupled with LC-MS/MS and metabolomics annotation, the authors identify active principles and use network pharmacology to predict their mechanisms of action against neuronal injury. The work supports the potential of this seaweed as a source of brain-healthy functional food ingredients.

papers.title: Syndirella: synthesis-directed fragment elaboration enables extensive and cost-effective binding site exploration beyond catalog compounds.
papers.abstract: Fragment screens provide an information-rich starting point for designing derivative compounds in structure-based drug discovery. However, derivatives in the fragment-to-hit stage are typically designed from only one or a few fragments, risking premature convergence on an unproductive series and dramatically limiting exploration of the binding site's interaction opportunities. This is avoidable by exploring a broad, chemically diverse set of scaffolds and elaborations spanning interactions revealed across many fragments, as well as those not yet observed. Conventional catalog procurement makes
papers.summary: Syndirella is a computational tool that designs derivative compounds from fragment screening hits by combining synthesis-aware elaboration with broad scaffold exploration, rather than optimizing a single fragment series. This enables cost-effective exploration of binding site interactions across many chemically diverse fragments, reducing the risk of premature convergence on unproductive series.

papers.title: Single-Particle STORM Imaging Quantifies Coating Heterogeneity Among Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoparticles.
papers.abstract: Cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CNPs) are a potentially transformative biomimetic targeted-delivery platform, which can engage therapeutic targets through source-cell membrane protein functions or homotypic interactions. However, their therapeutic development is limited by the current inability to accurately resolve membrane coating completeness, and CNP particle-to-particle variation. Here, we introduce a STochastic Optical Reconstruction Microscopy (STORM)-based approach that resolves population composition and quantifies membrane coating coverage at the single-particle level. Applying i
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a STORM super-resolution imaging method to measure how completely individual cell membrane-coated nanoparticles are covered by their membrane coating, revealing substantial particle-to-particle heterogeneity that bulk assays cannot detect. The approach enables quantification of coating coverage and population composition at the single-particle level, addressing a key barrier to the therapeutic development of these biomimetic delivery platforms.

papers.title: Structure-Based Engineering for PTPσ-Targeted Therapeutic Development.
papers.abstract: Protein tyrosine phosphatase sigma (PTPσ) is a member of the leukocyte common antigen-related (LAR) family of receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatases. Its architecture integrates an extracellular proteoglycan-sensing region, a single-pass transmembrane helix, and tandem intracellular phosphatase domains. In neural injury, inhibition of PTPσ signaling can relieve chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan (CSPG)-mediated restriction of axonal growth and plasticity. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), by contrast, restoration of PTPσ activity in fibroblast-like synoviocytes can suppress pathogenic migration
papers.summary: This review discusses structure-based protein engineering strategies to develop therapeutics targeting PTPσ, a receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatase. The authors highlight the dual therapeutic context: inhibiting PTPσ signaling to promote axonal regeneration after neural injury, versus restoring PTPσ activity to suppress pathogenic synoviocyte migration in rheumatoid arthritis. The paper synthesizes structural insights into PTPσ's extracellular proteoglycan-sensing region and intracellular phosphatase domains to guide rational drug design.

papers.title: Fixed Nonsynonymous vOka Vaccine Mutations in IE62 drive Varicella-Zoster Virus Attenuation in Human Skin.
papers.abstract: The live, attenuated vaccine for Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV) protects against chickenpox in children and adults. However, the vaccine strain Oka (vOka) establishes latency and may reactivate. The molecular basis of vOka attenuation remains unknown. We investigated whether three high-frequency single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that differentiate vOka from parental strain Oka (pOka) are responsible: S628G and R958G in the immediate-early regulatory protein IE62, and *130R in the membrane protein ORF0. We evaluated how these fixed SNPs mediate the attenuated growth phenotype of VZV and dimi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study identifies three fixed nonsynonymous mutations that distinguish the attenuated varicella-zoster vaccine strain (vOka) from its parental strain, focusing on two mutations in the immediate-early regulatory protein IE62 (S628G, R958G) and one in the membrane protein ORF0. Using human skin tissue models, the authors show that the IE62 mutations are the primary drivers of the vaccine's attenuated growth phenotype, providing a molecular explanation for how the live vaccine is weakened while remaining immunogenic.

papers.title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis.
papers.abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics
papers.summary: This study reports crystal structures of yeast aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS) bound to its substrate, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, to reveal how protein dynamics initiate heme biosynthesis. The work provides structural insight into the conformational changes that accompany substrate binding in this PLP-dependent enzyme, helping explain how ALAS homologs with ~70% sequence similarity diverge functionally. These findings offer a molecular framework for understanding ALAS regulation and the effects of disease-causing mutations.

papers.title: Harnessing the ubiquitin-proteasome system: advances and challenges of PROTACs in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most significant health issues in the world, and resistance to treatment and a lack of targets that can be addressed with drugs limit the effectiveness of the existing treatment options. The development of proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) has shifted the concept of occupancy-based inhibition toward event-based targeted protein degradation. Avoiding ubiquitin-proteasome hijacking, PROTACs target disease-relevant proteins to E3 ligases, allowing them to be catalytically degraded, thereby eliminating formerly undruggable or resistant targets. Their modular desi
papers.summary: This review examines proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) as an emerging therapeutic strategy for breast cancer, shifting from occupancy-based inhibition to event-based targeted protein degradation. PROTACs recruit disease-relevant proteins to E3 ligases for catalytic degradation, potentially addressing previously undruggable or treatment-resistant targets. The authors discuss advances and remaining challenges in applying this approach to breast cancer.

papers.title: Different dynamic behaviors between asymmetric catenanes and bonded rings.
papers.abstract: A hybrid mesoscopic simulation scheme integrating multi-particle collision dynamics (MPCD) and molecular dynamics (MD) was adopted to probe the dynamic responses and conformational evolution of semi-flexible asymmetric mechanically linked ([2]catenanes, PC) and chemically bonded (bonded rings, BR) ring polymers with different linkage modes under shear flow fields. First, by analyzing the prolateness, asphericity, and three-dimensional surface area of the ring, we reveal that the rings of asymmetric PC and BR adopt an identical conformation as a disc-like structure, whereas the symmetric PC and
papers.summary: This study uses hybrid mesoscopic simulations (MPCD + MD) to compare how asymmetric mechanically linked catenanes and chemically bonded ring polymers respond to shear flow. Both asymmetric architectures adopt similar disc-like conformations, but their dynamic responses and conformational evolution differ due to the linkage mode. The work clarifies how topology (mechanical linkage vs. covalent bonding) affects polymer dynamics under flow.

papers.title: Zinc peroxide-coated gold nanorods as the therapeutic adjuvants for photothermal enhanced chemodynamic therapy and metalloimmunotherapy against tumor.
papers.abstract: Traditional tumor therapies have limited efficacy, leading to a high mortality rate. Although immunotherapy holds considerable therapeutic promise, clinical immunotherapy for solid tumors only elicits durable responses in a minority of patients. This limitation is largely attributed to the highly immunosuppressive nature of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Notably, conventional chemodynamic therapy (CDT) is hampered by endogenous hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) shortage in tumor cells, and AZP compensates this defect via in-situ H2O2 self-supplementation to amplify hydroxyl radical generation.
papers.summary: This study develops zinc peroxide-coated gold nanorods (AZP) as a multifunctional therapeutic adjuvant for cancer treatment. The zinc peroxide coating self-supplies hydrogen peroxide within tumor cells, overcoming a key limitation of chemodynamic therapy, while the gold nanorods enable photothermal therapy. Together these effects amplify hydroxyl radical generation and stimulate metalloimmunotherapy, potentially reversing the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment to improve solid tumor treatment.

papers.title: Accelerating the discovery of nanoporous gas separation materials via Coulomb-enhanced classical density functional theory.
papers.abstract: The design of advanced nanoporous materials for gas separations, such as carbon capture and alkyne purification, is increasingly driven by high-throughput screening. However, the accurate description of electrostatic interactions in porous frameworks remains challenging and can introduce sizable deviations between predicted and experimental performance, thereby hindering rational materials design. To address this gap, we present a computational framework, compatible with standard force fields under appropriate charge assignments, that explicitly incorporates a point-charge model to capture ads
papers.summary: The paper presents a computational framework that combines classical density functional theory with an explicit point-charge model to better capture electrostatic interactions in nanoporous materials used for gas separations like carbon capture and alkyne purification. This approach aims to reduce the gap between predicted and experimental separation performance, enabling more reliable high-throughput screening of candidate materials.

papers.title: Integrated Experimental and Computational Investigation of Fluorinated Benzoylthiourea Derivatives: Structural Characterization, Hirshfeld Surface Analysis, Antioxidant Activity, and MAO-B Inhibitory Potential for Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Three novel fluorinated benzoylthiourea derivatives, namely FBTU1-FBTU3, were successfully synthesized in 79-86% yields and fully characterized using spectroscopic techniques including FT-IR, 1H, 13C and 19F NMR, UV-Vis spectroscopy, elemental analysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD). All three compounds crystallize in the monoclinic system (P21/c for FBTU1 and FBTU3; P21/n for FBTU2) with Z = 4. The crystallographic analysis revealed well-defined molecular geometries stabilized by intramolecular and intermolecular interactions. Hirshfeld surface and energy framework analyses ind
papers.summary: Three new fluorinated benzoylthiourea compounds were synthesized and structurally characterized using spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography, revealing their molecular packing and intermolecular interactions via Hirshfeld surface analysis. The compounds were also evaluated for antioxidant activity and MAO-B inhibition, a target relevant to Parkinson's disease, though the abstract does not report the quantitative results of these assays. This is a chemistry-focused structure-activity study of a small set of novel compounds.

papers.title: Integration of Network Toxicology and Machine Learning to Prioritize Candidate Molecular Features Associated with NNK-Related Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: 4-(Methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone (NNK) is a tobacco-specific nitrosamine implicated in tobacco-related lung carcinogenesis. Its biological effects in vivo depend substantially on metabolic conversion to NNAL and cytochrome P450-mediated formation of reactive intermediates. In this study, predicted NNK-associated proteins were integrated with lung cancer transcriptomic data sets, followed by network analysis and machine-learning-based feature prioritization. Five genes, SNAI2, PLAU, DNMT3A, FAP, and CCNB1, were prioritized based on their contributions to the multigene classificati
papers.summary: This study combined network toxicology predictions of NNK-interacting proteins with lung cancer transcriptomic datasets, then applied network analysis and machine learning to prioritize candidate molecular features. Five genes (SNAI2, PLAU, DNMT3A, FAP, and CCNB1) emerged as top contributors to a multigene classification model linking NNK exposure to lung cancer. The work offers a computational framework for identifying exposure-relevant biomarkers, though experimental validation is not reported.

papers.title: Benchmarking Affinity-Based Docking for Irreversible Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitors: A Physics-Informed Reactivity Framework for Stereoselective Potency Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Irreversible organophosphorus inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) act by covalent phosphylation of the catalytic serine, yet their computational prioritization is often based on affinity scores from noncovalent docking. We benchmark that assumption against a curated set of measured human-AChE inhibition rate constants (n = 14; G-, V-, and organophosphate-pesticide classes, including a configuration-resolved VX pair). AutoDock Vina affinity (Spearman ρ = +0.12) and GNINA CNN scores (ρ = -0.40) do not provide statistically reliable potency rankings; explicit covalent docking also remains w
papers.summary: The authors tested whether standard noncovalent docking scores can rank the potency of irreversible organophosphorus acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, using a curated set of 14 measured inhibition rate constants including a stereoresolved VX pair. They found that AutoDock Vina affinity and GNINA CNN scores fail to reliably rank potency, and even explicit covalent docking remains limited. They propose a physics-informed reactivity framework that accounts for covalent chemistry to better prioritize stereoselective potency.

papers.title: Integrated In Silico Analysis Reveals ABC Transporter ATP-Binding Protein as a Therapeutic Target in Helicobacter pylori.
papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori remains a major cause of gastric diseases, while increasing antimicrobial resistance highlights the need for novel therapeutic targets. Here, we developed a comprehensive computational target-prioritization framework integrating Rosetta Stone domain-fusion analysis, subtractive genomics, metabolic pathway mapping, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify pathogen-specific drug targets in H. pylori J99. Twelve conserved domain families comprising 746 proteins were identified, and domain abundance showed a weak negative correlation with versatility
papers.summary: This study uses a computational pipeline combining domain-fusion analysis, subtractive genomics, metabolic pathway mapping, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics to prioritize drug targets in Helicobacter pylori J99. The authors identify an ABC transporter ATP-binding protein as a promising pathogen-specific therapeutic target, motivated by rising antimicrobial resistance in H. pylori.

papers.title: Exploring the Molecular Mechanism of Ganoderic Acid B for Insomnia Based on Metabolomics, Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Objective: Ganoderma lucidum, a fungus of the genus Ganoderma in the family Polyporaceae, is often used in traditional medicine for the treatment of insomnia and amnesia, etc. Ganoderic acid B, a characteristic lanostane-type triterpenoid isolated from Ganoderma lucidum, has been preliminarily verified to possess mild sedative activity in existing studies. This study aims to explore the potential regulatory mechanism of Ganoderic acid B against PCPA-induced insomnia-like damage via multiple preclinical research strategies, and provide preliminary molecular and experimental clues for subsequent
papers.summary: This study investigates how ganoderic acid B, a compound from the medicinal fungus Ganoderma lucidum, may alleviate insomnia. Using metabolomics, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation in a PCPA-induced insomnia model, the authors identify potential molecular targets and pathways underlying its sedative effects. The work provides preliminary mechanistic clues linking this natural compound to insomnia-related metabolic and signaling networks.

papers.title: An Active Learning Framework for PFAS-Free Surfactant Discovery in Firefighting Foams.
papers.abstract: The growing concerns over the environmental and health impacts of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in firefighting foams have necessitated the development of efficient discovery frameworks for eco-friendly alternatives. In this work, we demonstrate an integrated pipeline leveraging active learning and coarse-grained (CG) molecular dynamics simulations to explore the design space of single-tail hydrocarbon surfactants for inhibiting fuel transport across interfaces. We design a targeted chemical space of 12,124 CG surfactants, represented by latent vectors learned from molecular graph
papers.summary: The authors present an active learning pipeline that combines coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations with learned latent representations of molecular graphs to search a 12,124-compound space of single-tail hydrocarbon surfactants as PFAS-free alternatives for firefighting foams. The framework iteratively selects candidates that inhibit fuel transport across interfaces, demonstrating how simulation-driven active learning can accelerate discovery of eco-friendly surfactant replacements.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of Lasmiditan Binding to Human Serum Albumin: Site Preference, Structural Response, and Binding Energetics.
papers.abstract: Human serum albumin (HSA), the major transport protein in blood plasma, can substantially influence the distribution of therapeutic compounds. Although lasmiditan (LASMI) is a recently introduced antimigraine drug with reported moderate plasma protein binding, the molecular determinants of its association with HSA remain poorly defined. Here, an integrated spectroscopic and computational approach was used to characterize HSA-LASMI complex formation, binding-site preference, and the accompanying structural response of the protein. UV-Vis absorption, steady-state fluorescence quenching, FTIR, an
papers.summary: This study characterizes how the antimigraine drug lasmiditan binds to human serum albumin using spectroscopy and computational modeling. The authors identify the preferred binding site, describe the structural changes HSA undergoes upon drug binding, and quantify the binding energetics. The work clarifies the molecular basis of lasmiditan's moderate plasma protein binding.

papers.title: Structural insights into the ligand modulation of MRGPRX4 conformational plasticity.
papers.abstract: Chronic pruritus is a debilitating condition with limited treatment options, particularly in cholestatic liver diseases, where bile acid dysregulation is a known trigger. Although Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X4 (MRGPRX4) has recently been identified as a key mediator of bile acid-induced pruritus, the structural mechanisms underlying its inhibition remain poorly understood, hindering the development of therapeutic antagonists. Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structures of MRGPRX4 in three distinct states: agonist-bound state, antagonist-bound state, and apo state. Our s
papers.summary: The authors solved cryo-EM structures of the itch receptor MRGPRX4 in agonist-bound, antagonist-bound, and apo states, revealing how ligand binding reshapes the receptor's conformation. This provides a structural basis for designing antagonists to treat bile acid-induced chronic pruritus in cholestatic liver disease.

papers.title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of AKT1 and structure-based drug design by buckwheat derived compounds.
papers.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Sheikh et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. AKT1 is a serine-threonine protein-kinase involved in tumour cell proliferation, survival, metabolism, and therapeutic resistance via activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. However, the comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of AKT1 and systematics identifications of natural AKT1 inhibitors remains limited. T
papers.summary: This study performs a pan-cancer integrative analysis of AKT1, a kinase in the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, to characterize its expression and clinical relevance across tumor types. The authors then use structure-based drug design to screen buckwheat-derived natural compounds as potential AKT1 inhibitors. The work combines multi-omics tumor analysis with computational docking to nominate plant-derived candidates for AKT1 targeting.

papers.title: Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand-bound protein complexes and ranking them by affinity are central problems in drug discovery. While deep-learning co-folding methods can help address these challenges, their evaluation has been hampered by the difficulties in assessing independence from training data and insufficiently large test sets. Here, we test the ability of co-folding methods to predict the structures of 551 ligands, 489 of which are of sufficient quality for evaluation, bound to the SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 macrodomain (Mac1) that were determined after the training cutoff dates. AlphaFold3 (AF3), Bo
papers.summary: This study prospectively evaluated deep-learning co-folding methods on 489 newly determined Mac1–ligand complexes (released after model training cutoffs) and across three virtual screens. AlphaFold3 and related methods were tested for both structure prediction and affinity-based ranking, providing a rare training-data-independent benchmark. The results clarify how well co-folding generalizes to unseen ligand-bound complexes and how useful it is for virtual screening.

papers.title: PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal-Binding Site and Type Prediction.
papers.abstract: Metal binding to proteins is crucial for many biological functions, yet the prediction of metal-binding sites and metal types remains underexplored compared to other biomolecular interactions. Despite advances in deep learning, computational methods have achieved limited success in this area; even the best-reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy on high-resolution crystal structures, and even worse when applied to medium-resolution data. We hypothesize that the main challenge lies in the nature of metal binding. While the putative sites span the entire protein surface, ac
papers.summary: The authors present PrOMet, a deep learning method for predicting metal-binding sites and metal types in proteins. They argue that the main difficulty is that candidate binding sites span the entire protein surface while actual binding events are sparse, and their approach improves localization accuracy over prior methods, including on medium-resolution structures. This addresses an underexplored protein interaction prediction task with practical relevance to structural and functional annotation.

papers.title: Advancing genetic pathogenicity prediction with three-dimensional proteoform-phenotype analysis.
papers.abstract: Ascertaining the pathogenicity and clinical relevance of genetic mutations is a longstanding challenge across human disease. This is particularly relevant for genes with many variants of unknown significance (VUS), such as PRPH2-retinopathy, where complex variable phenotype patterns and limited genotype correlations hinder application of precision-medicine therapies. Recent AI-based pathogenicity tools, while powerful, may be limited by insufficient mechanistic or phenotypic training data. We established a three-dimensional proteoform-phenotype analysis framework by combining AI-generated prot
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors present a framework for predicting genetic variant pathogenicity by combining AI-generated protein structural models with phenotypic data, applied to PRPH2-retinopathy where many variants of unknown significance complicate diagnosis. The approach links three-dimensional proteoform features to clinical phenotypes to improve pathogenicity classification beyond existing AI tools that lack mechanistic or phenotypic training data. This offers a potential route to better variant interpretation for genes with complex genotype-phenotype relationships.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the fungus-specific antifungal protein NFAP2 as a guide to identify its intracellular targets in Candida albicans (including glutamate decarboxylase and mitochondrial ATP synthase) and then applies structure-based drug repurposing to find existing compounds that hit these targets. The approach aims to accelerate antifungal development by leveraging drugs with known safety profiles against a pathogen with limited treatment options and rising resistance.

papers.title: Atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from Escherichia coli by cryo-EM and solid-state NMR.
papers.abstract: Mechanosensitive channels are central to cellular responses to membrane tension, yet the structural basis of their gating remains incompletely understood. Here, we determine the structures of wild-type and Gly22→Ser (G22S) mutants of MscL from Escherichia coli (EcMscL) by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) in peptide-based lipid nanodiscs and complement them with solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements in liposomes to capture their dynamics in a native-like membrane environment. The cryo-EM structures reveal a closed conformation, whereas analysis of the low-threshold G2
papers.summary: The study presents cryo-EM structures of wild-type and G22S mutant E. coli MscL in lipid nanodiscs, revealing a closed conformation, complemented by solid-state NMR in liposomes to probe membrane-embedded dynamics. This combined approach provides atomic-level insight into the structural basis of mechanosensitive channel gating in a native-like lipid environment.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Network Analysis Identifies Candidate Kinase-Mediated Thyroid-Associated Targets of Withaferin A.
papers.abstract: Withaferin A (WA), a bioactive steroidal lactone derived from Withania somnifera, has been reported to exhibit diverse pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory effects. Although previous studies suggest a potential link between WA and thyroid-related molecular pathways, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed a comprehensive computational approach to explore WA-responsive molecular changes potentially relevant to thyroid-associated processes. RNA-sequencing data from WA-treated MCF-10A human mam
papers.summary: This study uses computational analysis of RNA-sequencing data from Withaferin A-treated MCF-10A cells combined with network analysis to identify candidate kinase-mediated molecular targets potentially relevant to thyroid-associated pathways. The work proposes a set of WA-responsive genes and kinases as hypotheses for the compound's thyroid-related effects, though the findings are computational predictions requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: In vivo fate-guided design of efficient delivery systems for PROTACs: From molecular rationales to clinical progress.
papers.abstract: Despite two decades of intensive molecular engineering, the clinical translation of proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) remains constrained by a fundamental paradox: high in vitro potency often fails to translate into in vivo efficacy due to poor pharmacokinetics (PK)/pharmacodynamics (PD) profiles and uncontrolled biodistribution. This review departs from conventional narratives centered on potency by introducing a framework focused on drug fate that explicitly connects the absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion (ADME), and tumor targeting of PROTACs with the rational design of
papers.summary: This review reframes PROTAC development around drug fate rather than potency, arguing that poor pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and uncontrolled biodistribution—not weak target engagement—are the main barriers to clinical translation. It connects ADME properties and tumor-targeting behavior to the rational design of delivery systems, and surveys progress from molecular rationale to clinical-stage candidates.

papers.title: Fluorination: A strategy to tune the interactions of molecules and nanoscale systems with biological matter.
papers.abstract: Fluorination has become a key molecular engineering strategy in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine, enabling the fine tuning of the physicochemical and biological properties of therapeutic molecules and drug delivery systems. The unique characteristics of fluorine, including its small steric footprint, high electronegativity, and exceptional strength of the C-F bond, enhance metabolic stability, modulate lipophilicity and acidity, and improve pharmacokinetic profiles. Beyond these well-established effects, fluorination has emerged as a tool for controlling the assembly and biological behavio
papers.summary: This review argues that adding fluorine atoms to therapeutic molecules and nanoscale drug-delivery systems is a powerful way to fine-tune how they interact with biological systems. Fluorine's small size, high electronegativity, and strong carbon-fluorine bond improve metabolic stability, lipophilicity, acidity, and pharmacokinetics, and can also control molecular assembly and biological behavior. The authors frame fluorination as a general molecular-engineering strategy for medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine.

papers.title: Phytochemical Profiling, In Vitro α-Amylase Inhibitory and Antioxidant Activities of Madhuca longifolia Leaf and Bark Extracts with Molecular Docking Analysis.
papers.abstract: Plant-derived phytochemicals are increasingly investigated for their antioxidant and enzyme-inhibitory activities as potential sources of bioactive compounds. The present study evaluated the phytochemical composition, antioxidant activity, and in vitro α-amylase inhibitory activity of Madhuca longifolia leaf and bark extracts, followed by GC-MS profiling and exploratory computational analyses of the methanolic leaf fraction. Moreover, we elucidated the ADME properties of GC-MS-putatively identified compounds and their computational molecular interactions with α-amylase. The leaves and barks we
papers.summary: This study profiles the phytochemical composition of Madhuca longifolia leaf and bark extracts using GC-MS and evaluates their antioxidant and α-amylase inhibitory activities in vitro. The authors then use molecular docking and ADME predictions to explore how putatively identified compounds might interact with α-amylase, suggesting potential antidiabetic bioactivity. The work is exploratory and relies on computational predictions rather than in vivo validation.

papers.title: Protein Language Models Identify Early Folding Residues as Critical Hotspots for Pathogenic Variants and Cancer Prognosis.
papers.abstract: Identifying the specific residues that initiate protein folding is critical for understanding protein stability and the mechanisms of misfolding-related diseases. However, the systematic, proteome-wide identification of these early folding residues (EFRs) has been hampered by both experimental and computational limitations. Here, we present LMEFold, a deep learning framework using protein language models (PLMs) to accurately predict EFRs from amino acid sequence alone. LMEFold outperforms existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831), and its predicted scores
papers.summary: The authors present LMEFold, a deep learning framework that uses protein language models to predict early folding residues (EFRs) directly from amino acid sequence, outperforming existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831). They then show that these predicted EFRs are enriched for pathogenic variants and are associated with cancer prognosis, suggesting folding-initiation sites are functional hotspots.

papers.title: Enhancing the Activity of Ribokinase from Thermus sp. 2.9 Through Rational Design for the Cascade Synthesis of Modified Nucleotides and Nucleosides.
papers.abstract: The pursuit of efficient approaches for the production of promising antiviral and cytostatic pharmaceuticals is a crucial direction in medical biotechnology, especially after the COVID-19 pandemic. Modified nucleosides and nucleotides represent a highly promising class of chemicals for the development of drugs against cancer and viral infections. Being an alternative to traditional chemical synthesis, cascades of nucleic exchange enzymes offer single-step synthesis of such compounds with exceptional stereo- and regioselectivity. Furthermore, employing thermostable enzymes for such cascades off
papers.summary: The authors used rational design to engineer a more active ribokinase from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus sp. 2.9, aiming to improve a multi-enzyme cascade for producing modified nucleosides and nucleotides, which are valuable antiviral and anticancer drug precursors. The engineered enzyme is intended to enable more efficient single-step, stereoselective synthesis of these compounds compared to traditional chemical routes. The work highlights thermostable enzymes as practical biocatalysts for pharmaceutical nucleotide production.

papers.title: Antioxidant Activity and Anti-Inflammatory Potential of Rhododendron dauricum Flowers via UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS Combined with Network Pharmacology and In Vitro Validation.
papers.abstract: Rhododendron dauricum L. flowers are highly valued as ornamental plants in northern Chinese horticulture, yet while its leaves are well-known for their antitussive and anti-asthmatic effects, the flowers themselves remain an underutilized resource. Oxidative stress and chronic inflammation are intimately intertwined pathological processes that mutually reinforce each other in a self-perpetuating cycle, and current clinical treatments for diseases related to oxidative stress and inflammation have become a significant focus of research. This study investigated the chemical composition and bioact
papers.summary: This study used UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS to profile the chemical constituents of Rhododendron dauricum flowers, then applied network pharmacology to predict antioxidant and anti-inflammatory targets and pathways, followed by in vitro assays to validate the predicted activities. The work positions the underutilized flowers as a source of bioactive compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory potential, supporting their further development beyond the ornamental value.

papers.title: The PTPN1/N2 Peptide Inhibitor Achieves Potent, Long-Acting Glycemic Control and Weight-Loss Dual Efficacy in Mice.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity are closely linked metabolic disorders driven by insulin and leptin resistance. Current long-acting therapies capable of addressing both conditions are dominated by incretin-based agents, which primarily achieve efficacy through appetite suppression and are frequently associated with tolerability limitations and metabolic rebound after treatment discontinuation. Alternative strategies that correct underlying signaling defects without suppressing food intake remain lacking. Protein tyrosine phosphatases PTPN1 and PTPN2 act as coordinated intracellular negati
papers.summary: This study describes a peptide inhibitor targeting PTPN1 and PTPN2, two phosphatases that negatively regulate insulin and leptin signaling. In mice, the inhibitor produced potent, long-lasting improvements in glycemic control and weight loss without relying on appetite suppression, offering a potential alternative to incretin-based therapies. The approach addresses underlying signaling defects rather than reducing food intake.

papers.title: Benzothiazole-Derived Compounds as Potential Drugs for the Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes: A Descriptive Review.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is a multifactorial metabolic disease in which hyperglycemia coexists with insulin resistance, β-cell dysfunction, dyslipidemia, and progressive microvascular and macrovascular complications. The structural versatility of the benzothiazole scaffold has enabled the development of a diverse array of preclinical compounds capable of modulating multiple diabetes-relevant targets. This review critically analyzes the available evidence on benzothiazole-derived compounds exhibiting antidiabetic or other diabetes-related pharmacological activities. No lower publication-date limit
papers.summary: This review surveys preclinical benzothiazole-derived compounds that show antidiabetic or diabetes-related pharmacological activity, covering their modulation of multiple targets relevant to type 2 diabetes such as hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and β-cell dysfunction. It critically analyzes the available evidence for this versatile scaffold as a source of candidate T2D therapeutics. The work is a descriptive synthesis of preclinical findings rather than new experimental data.

papers.title: Quantum Computing for Polymeric Composites: Principles, Methods, Applications, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Polymeric composites have become indispensable engineering materials owing to their exceptional mechanical performance, lightweight characteristics, corrosion resistance, and design flexibility. Conventional computational approaches, including density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML), have substantially improved the understanding of polymer structure-property relationships. However, the increasing complexity of multiscale polymeric systems, intricate fiber-matrix interactions, and the computational cost associated with a
papers.summary: This review surveys how quantum computing could be applied to polymeric composites, covering underlying principles, quantum algorithms, and potential applications alongside conventional DFT, MD, FEA, and ML methods. It argues that quantum approaches may help address the computational bottlenecks of modeling complex multiscale polymer systems and fiber-matrix interactions, and outlines future research directions.

papers.title: Conformational Sampling of CPT1A Enables Dynamic Structure-Based Ligand Screening.
papers.abstract: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A) catalyzes a rate-limiting step in fatty acid β-oxidation and is a target for studies of metabolic disease and cancer. However, the structural dynamics of CPT1A remain poorly understood due to the lack of full-length structure. In this study, we employed an integrated computational approach combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, Markov state models (MSMs), and binding free energy calculations to elucidate the conformational landscape of human CPT1A. We performed an all-atom MD simulation of CPT1A embedded in a realistic outer mitochondrial membr
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations, Markov state models, and binding free energy calculations to map the conformational landscape of human CPT1A, a key enzyme in fatty acid oxidation and a drug target for metabolic disease and cancer. Because no full-length CPT1A structure exists, the authors simulate the protein embedded in a realistic outer mitochondrial membrane to capture its dynamic behavior. The resulting conformational ensembles enable structure-based ligand screening against multiple CPT1A states rather than a single static structure.

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of Novel Peptides Targeting Protein Disulfide Isomerase as Antiplatelet Agents.
papers.abstract: Extracellular protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) is a critical mediator of thrombus formation and a promising target for novel antithrombotic therapies aiming to overcome the bleeding risks associated with current antiplatelet agents. This study aimed to design and evaluate novel, targeted peptide-based PDI inhibitors with a safe physiological profile. We utilized a bioinformatics-driven rational design approach, based on the evolutionary conservation of the PDI active site, to generate a library of 34 targeted peptides. The inhibitory mechanism and biological efficacy of the lead candidate, pe
papers.summary: The authors used evolutionary conservation of the PDI active site to rationally design 34 peptides targeting extracellular protein disulfide isomerase, a mediator of thrombus formation. They evaluated a lead candidate peptide as an antiplatelet agent with a potentially safer bleeding profile than current antithrombotics. The work presents a bioinformatics-guided peptide design pipeline for a promising antithrombotic target.

papers.title: Screening and identification of a novel umami peptide with in vitro anti-inflammatory potential from sea cucumber protein: Integration of flavoromics, bioinformatic prediction, molecular simulation and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Sea cucumber protein was sequentially hydrolyzed with pepsin, trypsin, and enterokinase to obtain peptides with desirable taste characteristics and immunomodulatory potential. Multi-scale characterization, flavoromics, peptidomics, bioinformatic screening, molecular simulations, and cellular assays were employed to investigate the structural changes, flavor remodeling, and bioactivity of the resulting hydrolysates. Results showed that hydrolysis disrupted the compact protein structure, induced conformational unfolding, and yielded short peptides (0.5-1.5 kDa) with enhanced hydrophilicity and p
papers.summary: This study used sequential enzymatic hydrolysis of sea cucumber protein to generate short peptides (0.5–1.5 kDa) with improved taste and immunomodulatory properties. By integrating flavoromics, peptidomics, bioinformatic screening, molecular simulations, and cellular assays, the authors identified a novel umami peptide with in vitro anti-inflammatory potential. The work demonstrates a multi-scale pipeline for discovering bioactive food-derived peptides that combine desirable flavor with health benefits.

papers.title: Graph-theoretic microstate analysis reveals altered dynamics in common-cation mixed electrolytes.
papers.abstract: Mixed aqueous electrolytes are increasingly valuable in industrial applications, where they often behave very differently from their single-salt counterparts, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we present a comprehensive molecular dynamics simulation study of ion networks in NaNO2(aq), NaNO3(aq), and their mixtures. New graph-theoretic workflows combined with principal component analysis identify ion aggregate macro-states, based on number of cations in the cluster, and microstates, based on inter-ion connectivity patterns, enabling detailed investigation of state tr
papers.summary: This paper uses molecular dynamics simulations and new graph-theoretic workflows combined with principal component analysis to characterize ion aggregation in single-salt and mixed aqueous electrolytes (NaNO2, NaNO3, and their mixtures). The authors identify macro-states based on cation counts and microstates based on inter-ion connectivity patterns, revealing altered dynamics in the mixed electrolytes compared to single-salt solutions. The approach offers a general framework for understanding how ion network structure and dynamics differ in complex electrolyte mixtures.

papers.title: Imidazo[1,2-b]Pyrazole-1,2,4-oxadiazole Linked 1,2,3-Triazoles: Synthesis, Antibacterial, Biofilm, and In Silico Studies.
papers.abstract: The growing incidence of bacterial resistance, especially in gram-positive infections, emphasizes how urgently new antibacterial medicines must be developed. This study presents the rational design and synthesis of a series of fused imidazo[1,2-b]pyrazole-1,2,4-oxadiazole-1,2,3-triazole hybrids (8a-8n) employing a multi-step synthetic approach that includes oxidative cyclisation, amidoxime formation, Vilsmeier-mediated cyclodehydration, and Cu(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC). The synthesized compounds were assessed for their in vitro antibacterial efficacy against Bacillus subt
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of 14 hybrid molecules combining imidazo[1,2-b]pyrazole, 1,2,4-oxadiazole, and 1,2,3-triazole scaffolds using a multi-step route including CuAAC click chemistry. These compounds were tested in vitro for antibacterial activity against Bacillus subtilis and other strains, with additional biofilm and in silico docking analyses. The work is a medicinal chemistry structure-activity exploration aimed at finding new agents against gram-positive bacterial infections.

papers.title: Green Extraction of Phenolic Compounds From Pistacia lentiscus Leaves Coupled With LC-MS Characterization and Structure-Based Enzyme Inhibition Analysis.
papers.abstract: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and urease are critical enzymes involved in various pathological conditions associated with cellular and tissue damage. Natural products are increasingly explored as safer alternatives to synthetic inhibitors. This study evaluates the phytochemical composition and enzyme inhibitory potential of Pistacia lentiscus leaves using a green extraction approach. Bioactive compounds were extracted via lactic acid-assisted ultrasound, and the crude extract was characterized for total phenolics, flavonoids, LC-MS profile, and in vitro inhibition of acetylcholinesterase and ure
papers.summary: This study uses a green lactic acid-assisted ultrasound extraction to obtain phenolic compounds from Pistacia lentiscus leaves, then characterizes them by LC-MS and tests their ability to inhibit acetylcholinesterase and urease. The work links phytochemical profiling with in vitro enzyme inhibition and structure-based analysis, suggesting the extract as a natural source of inhibitors relevant to pathologies involving these enzymes.

papers.title: DyME: An MD-based engine exploiting HTP mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry.
papers.abstract: Protein recognition mimicry (PRM) is of great interest in the field of molecular bioengineering and rational design, with mutagenesis frequently employed to analyze the effects of altering amino acids involved in molecular recognition. The conformational and energetic effects of such alterations can be investigated in detail with the help of molecular dynamics (MD) methodologies. While existing MD-based computational tools can be used to explore a particular set of mutations at a time, suitable for small-scale studies, high-throughput (HTP) exploration of protein recognition for engineering pu
papers.summary: DyME is a molecular dynamics-based computational engine designed to handle high-throughput mutagenesis studies for protein engineering and protein recognition mimicry. It addresses the limitation of existing MD tools that can only explore one set of mutations at a time, enabling large-scale exploration of how amino acid changes affect molecular recognition. This makes it possible to systematically screen many mutation combinations for rational design applications.

papers.title: Structural insights into an aptainhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 E protein using molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and biophysical analyses.
papers.abstract: The envelope (E) protein is a highly conserved structural protein that plays key roles in viral assembly, membrane curvature, and pathogenesis. The E-protein transmembrane (TM) domain oligomerizes into a pentameric ion channel, which contributes to the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome that is directly linked to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Therefore, targeted disruption of E-protein oligomerization represents a powerful therapeutic strategy to attenuate viral virulence. In this study, we report the first DNA aptainhibitors to block E-protein oligomerization. The lead aptainh
papers.summary: This study reports the first DNA aptamers designed to inhibit oligomerization of the SARS-CoV-2 envelope (E) protein transmembrane domain, which forms a pentameric ion channel linked to NLRP3 inflammasome activation and ARDS. Using molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and biophysical analyses, the authors characterize how the lead aptamer binds and disrupts E-protein assembly. The work proposes a therapeutic strategy to attenuate viral virulence by targeting E-protein oligomerization rather than the virus directly.

papers.title: Clodronate and trehalose exhibit a paradoxical antagonistic interaction that suppresses proliferation of canine mammary tumour cells.
papers.abstract: Clodronate and trehalose are known to modulate metabolic and autophagy-related pathways, respectively, yet their combined effects on tumour cell proliferation remain poorly understood. This study investigated the individual and combined effects of these compounds on the canine mammary tumour cell line CMT-U27 and explored underlying mechanisms using network pharmacology. Cell proliferation was assessed following treatment with clodronate, trehalose, and their combination across a range of concentrations. Growth rate analysis and Bliss independence modelling were used to evaluate drug interacti
papers.summary: This study tested clodronate and trehalose, alone and in combination, on a canine mammary tumour cell line (CMT-U27). Unexpectedly, the two compounds interacted antagonistically, suppressing tumour cell proliferation less than expected from their individual effects, and network pharmacology was used to explore the underlying mechanisms. The work highlights that combining metabolic and autophagy-modulating agents can produce counterintuitive interactions that matter for drug combination design.

papers.title: A single amino acid mutation alters substrate specificity towards l-glucose in a bacterial l-galactose dehydrogenase.
papers.abstract: Structure-based mutagenesis was performed to modify the substrate specificity of bacterial l-galactose dehydrogenase from Luteolibacter sp. strain LG18, which also exhibits intrinsic l-glucose dehydrogenase activity. Based on previously reported crystal structures of the enzyme in ternary complex with l-galactose or l-glucose and NADP+, an M212Q mutant was generated and found to exhibit a pronounced preference for l-glucose. Kinetic analysis showed that the M212Q mutant displayed an approximately 20-fold higher k cat/K M value for l-glucose than for l-galactose. To elucidate the structural bas
papers.summary: Researchers used structure-based mutagenesis to alter the substrate specificity of a bacterial L-galactose dehydrogenase that also has intrinsic L-glucose dehydrogenase activity. The M212Q mutation shifted the enzyme's preference toward L-glucose, yielding a ~20-fold higher catalytic efficiency (kcat/KM) for L-glucose over L-galactose. This demonstrates that a single amino acid substitution can substantially redirect substrate specificity in this enzyme family.

papers.title: Rational structure-guided identification of a Bcl-2-targeting peptide with antiproliferative effects on colorectal cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Bcl-2 is critical for tumour survival and serves as a promising anticancer drug target. Herein, a series of novel Bcl-2-targeted peptides were identified through structure-based virtual screening and systematic biological validation. Four candidate peptides were selected from the peptide library. MST results demonstrated that Peptide 1 exhibited the strongest apparent binding affinity towards Bcl-2 (Kd = 0.51 ± 0.03 μM), superior to VS-9 and other screened peptides. Molecular dynamics simulation, free energy landscape analysis, and MM/GBSA calculation further supported the predicted conformati
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify peptides that bind the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2, then validated the top candidates experimentally. Peptide 1 showed the strongest binding affinity (Kd ≈ 0.51 μM) and inhibited proliferation of colorectal cancer cells, with molecular dynamics simulations supporting the predicted binding mode. This provides a starting point for developing peptide-based Bcl-2 inhibitors as anticancer agents.

papers.title: Potential Molecular Links Between Benzophenone-3 and Breast Cancer: Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Molecular Modeling, and Gene Expression Validation.
papers.abstract: Benzophenone-3 (BP-3) is a widely used ultraviolet filter with potential carcinogenic concern, but its molecular link with breast cancer remains unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate targets and potential molecular links between BP-3 and breast cancer using toxicological prediction, machine learning, molecular modeling, and gene expression analysis.
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, molecular docking/modeling, and gene expression analysis to identify candidate molecular targets linking the UV filter benzophenone-3 (BP-3) to breast cancer. It proposes potential target genes and pathways through which BP-3 exposure might contribute to breast carcinogenesis, offering hypotheses for future experimental validation.

papers.title: Mechanism of luteolin in treating chronic heart failure by regulating HIF-1 signaling pathway-mediated mitochondrial damage to inhibit cardiomyocyte apoptosis.
papers.abstract: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is a systemic cardiovascular disease characterized by an extremely poor prognosis. Luteolin demonstrates promising therapeutic potential in the prevention and management of CHF. This study aims to explore the mechanism by which luteolin ameliorates CHF through mitigating mitochondrial damage and inhibiting cardiomyocyte apoptosis, using bioinformatics analysis combined with in vitro and in vivo experiments.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study combines bioinformatics with in vitro and in vivo experiments to show that luteolin alleviates chronic heart failure by modulating the HIF-1 signaling pathway, which reduces mitochondrial damage and inhibits cardiomyocyte apoptosis. The findings suggest a mechanistic rationale for luteolin as a potential therapeutic agent in CHF.

papers.title: Artificially intelligent modeling of macromolecular assemblies.
papers.abstract: The study of macromolecular assembly formation is one of the most challenging tasks in computational modeling as it requires extensive exploration of conformational and configurational space, especially when driven by conformational transitions or folding instabilities, which are typically associated with high energy barriers. Although this type of study has traditionally been addressed in silico by using techniques that reduce the computational cost of simulations, such as coarse-grained models, artificial intelligence (AI) has recently entered the field at multiple levels, aiding in paramete
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence is being integrated into computational modeling of macromolecular assembly formation, a problem that requires exploring vast conformational and configurational spaces often hindered by high energy barriers. It covers AI applications at multiple levels, including aiding parameterization and potentially reducing reliance on traditional coarse-grained simulation techniques. The paper surveys the current state and future directions of AI-driven approaches for this challenging structural biology problem.

papers.title: Correction: Metals-triggered compound CDPDP exhibits anti-arthritic behavior by downregulating the inflammatory cytokines, and modulating the oxidative storm in mice models with extensive ADMET, docking and simulation studies.
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.3389/fphar.2022.1053744.].
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article on the compound CDPDP, which was reported to have anti-arthritic effects in mice by reducing inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress, supported by ADMET, docking, and simulation analyses. The correction likely addresses errors or omissions in the original publication, but the abstract provides no details on the nature of the correction or any new findings.

papers.title: Exploring the potential targets and possible mechanisms of Shenqi Fuzheng Injection in the treatment of cancer-associated muscle wasting based on network pharmacology.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated muscle wasting (CAMW) is a debilitating condition observed in cancer patients, characterized by progressive skeletal muscle loss driven by tumor-secreted inflammatory cytokines, metabolic reprogramming, and enhanced apoptotic signaling, severely affecting the quality of life of patients. Shenqi Fuzheng Injection (SFI) is a traditional Chinese medicine preparation made from Codonopsis pilosula (Dangshen) and Astragalus membranaceus (Huangqi) in specific proportions, which has the effects of replenishing qi, strengthening the body, alleviating the side effects of radiotherapy a
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology to predict the molecular targets and mechanisms by which Shenqi Fuzheng Injection (a traditional Chinese medicine made from Codonopsis pilosula and Astragalus membranaceus) may treat cancer-associated muscle wasting. The authors identify candidate targets and pathways linking the herbal compounds to the inflammatory, metabolic, and apoptotic processes driving muscle loss, providing hypotheses for future experimental validation.

papers.title: Mechanistic study on components of Angelica Pubescens-Taxillus Chinensis in improving compression-induced intervertebral disc degeneration via piezo1/NF-κB signaling axis.
papers.abstract: Abnormal mechanical load is a critical risk factor for intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), and nucleus pulposus (NP) cell senescence is a core pathogenic mechanism in IVDD. Piezo1 is a mechanosensitive ion channel, whereas the NF-κB pathway promotes cellular senescence. The classical formula Duhuo Jisheng decoction has shown potential benefits in IVDD-related conditions, and its core herbal pair Angelica Pubescens-Taxillus Chinensis accounting for its pivotal therapeutic effects.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how the herbal pair Angelica Pubescens-Taxillus Chinensis (from Duhuo Jisheng decoction) protects against compression-induced intervertebral disc degeneration. The authors propose that the mechanism involves modulation of the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 and the NF-κB senescence pathway in nucleus pulposus cells. The work is a mechanistic pharmacology study of a traditional Chinese medicine formula in a specific disease context.

papers.title: Peptide optimization to improve antigen presentation and antitumor responses in sarcoma.
papers.abstract: Sarcomas are rare and heterogeneous malignancies for which therapeutic options remain limited, particularly in advanced disease. Standard treatments, including surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and approved targeted agents, provide marginal improvements in progression-free and overall survival, highlighting the need for immunotherapeutic strategies. Therapeutic cancer vaccines represent a promising strategy, but clinical efficacy has been limited by low antigen immunogenicity and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Enhancing antigen presentation and T-cell receptor (TCR) enga
papers.summary: This paper describes peptide optimization strategies aimed at improving antigen presentation and T-cell receptor engagement for sarcoma cancer vaccines. The authors argue that poor antigen immunogenicity and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment have limited vaccine efficacy, and propose peptide engineering as a route to stronger antitumor immune responses. The work is preclinical/translational in scope and focuses on a rare, heterogeneous cancer type.

papers.title: Integrated toxicogenomic and single-nucleus transcriptomic analyses prioritize SDHB and NDUFAB1 in mitochondrial respiration-associated remodeling during cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury (Cis-AKI) is a multifactorial nephrotoxic syndrome involving proximal tubular injury, oxidative and inflammatory stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, metabolic disturbance, and regulated cell death. However, the molecular targets linking cisplatin-associated toxicogenomic changes to AKI remain incompletely characterized.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates toxicogenomic data with single-nucleus transcriptomics to identify molecular drivers of mitochondrial dysfunction in cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury. The authors prioritize SDHB and NDUFAB1 as key genes involved in mitochondrial respiration-associated remodeling during Cis-AKI. The work highlights mitochondrial respiratory chain components as potential targets linking cisplatin toxicity to kidney injury.

papers.title: Discovery of metabolite biomarkers for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury based on metabolomics: neurotoxic mechanism and functional validation of a flavopiridol -related metabolite.
papers.abstract: To investigate the role and potential mechanism of metabolite alterations during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) and to explore novel candidate molecular markers for the diagnosis of this disease.
papers.summary: This study uses metabolomics to identify metabolite biomarkers associated with cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). The authors highlight a flavopiridol-related metabolite and provide functional validation of its neurotoxic mechanism, suggesting it may serve as a diagnostic marker for CIRI.

papers.title: Mapping the major B-cell linear epitope of silkworm (Bombyx mori) pupal chitinase and molecular dynamics insights into its IgE-binding stability.
papers.abstract: As domestic silkworm (Bombyx mori) pupae emerge as a promising alternative food source, the severe IgE-mediated allergic reactions they trigger have raised significant public health concerns. Despite the identification of the novel allergen Bombyx mori chitinase (BmChi), its precise linear B-cell epitopes and molecular mechanisms of IgE recognition remain uncharacterized. In this hypothesis-generating study, we systematically mapped the linear B-cell epitopes of BmChi and evaluated their structural dynamics. Following bioinformatic predictions, a high-resolution in vitro screening using 109 ov
papers.summary: This study maps the linear B-cell epitopes of Bombyx mori pupal chitinase (BmChi), a newly identified allergen in silkworm pupae that are being explored as an alternative food source. Using bioinformatic predictions followed by in vitro screening of overlapping peptides, the authors identify a major IgE-binding epitope and use molecular dynamics simulations to assess the stability of its interaction with IgE. The work provides the first epitope-level characterization of BmChi, which could inform allergen risk assessment and detection for silkworm-derived foods.

papers.title: Structure-based discovery of a novel Granzyme A (GZMA) inhibitor for autism spectrum disorder through integrative transcriptomics, virtual screening, and long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Granzyme A (GZMA) is a trypsin-like serine protease expressed in cytotoxic lymphocytes that cleaves gasdermin B (GSDMB) to release a pore-forming N-terminal fragment, thereby inducing pyroptosis, a lytic and pro-inflammatory form of programmed cell death. This pathway has been implicated in immune dysregulation reported in a subset of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In this study, we reanalyzed the peripheral blood transcriptome dataset GSE26415 using an integrative computational framework comprising outlier-aware quality control, differential expression analysis, functional e
papers.summary: The authors reanalyzed a peripheral blood transcriptome dataset from autism spectrum disorder (ASD) patients and identified Granzyme A (GZMA) as a potential therapeutic target linked to immune dysregulation and pyroptosis. They then used virtual screening and long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations to discover a novel small-molecule inhibitor of GZMA, proposing it as a candidate treatment for a subset of ASD patients. The work is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation.

papers.title: Underpinning hierarchical anisotropic structure formation in soy protein high-moisture extrudates by Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
papers.abstract: Plant-based meat alternatives are fibrous anisotropic food protein products that mimic the texture and palatability of animal-based foods. The main industrially scalable production technique for manufacturing such structured protein materials is high-moisture extrusion, which involves the thermo-mechanical processing, and subsequent cooling, of a hot protein melt in the presence of shear and temperature gradients. Yet, the complex mechanisms governing fibrous structure formation in plant-protein extrudates are poorly characterised, in turn limiting the rational design and optimisation of the e
papers.summary: This study uses Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) to visualize how hierarchical anisotropic structures form in soy protein high-moisture extrudates, a key process for making plant-based meat alternatives. The work provides new insight into the fibrous structure formation mechanisms during thermo-mechanical processing, which have been poorly characterized and limit rational design of meat analogs.

papers.title: Nanozymes in Tumor Microenvironment Modulation for Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central regulatory role in malignant tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, and its complexity and dynamic heterogeneity markedly limit the efficacy of current treatment strategies. Therefore, the development of novel functional materials capable of effectively remodeling the TME and alleviating immunosuppression and therapeutic tolerance has become an important research direction in cancer therapy. In recent years, nanozymes, as a class of nanomaterials with enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity, have shown broad potential in TME intervention and
papers.summary: This review discusses nanozymes—nanomaterials that mimic enzyme catalytic activity—as tools to remodel the tumor microenvironment for cancer therapy. It highlights how these materials can intervene in TME complexity and heterogeneity to alleviate immunosuppression and therapeutic resistance, though the abstract is truncated and specific findings are not detailed.
